theme: Domain-driven design, messaging and event sourcing in a small .NET equipment-rental core (Lending and Billing bounded contexts)

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The Loan aggregate holds the Member aggregate itself (an EF navigation) instead of its MemberId. Loading or saving a loan now drags the member into the loan's consistency boundary: a change saved through the loan can write member state, and the two can no longer be stored, locked or scaled apart.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The loaned equipment unit is identified by a raw Guid although the domain has an EquipmentUnitId type: a LoanId, MemberId or EquipmentId Guid can be passed where a unit id is meant and the compiler cannot tell.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The published integration event carries the Lending domain's own UnitCondition enum, so the contracts assembly references Rentals.Lending.Domain and every consumer (Billing) compiles against the producer's domain model: renaming or adding a condition in Lending is a breaking change for other contexts.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Reservation is an aggregate root with state and no behaviour: confirming, cancelling and the window and member-standing rules all live in ReservationService, which sets its properties directly. Nothing on the aggregate protects its invariants (any caller can set a cancelled reservation back to Confirmed).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Member.Tier has a public setter next to ChangeTier, which also adjusts the loan limit. Any caller can assign the tier and leave LoanLimit inconsistent with it, bypassing the aggregate's own method.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Every property of the Reservation aggregate (member, equipment, window, status) has a public setter; the status can be moved from Cancelled back to Confirmed by assignment.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The Member aggregate carries EF Core's [Index] attribute (Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore), so the domain project references the ORM to express a database index. Persistence mapping belongs in the infrastructure configuration, where the other aggregates' mappings already are.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A domain service takes an EF Core DbContext and queries the Loans set itself: the domain layer reaches the database directly instead of through a repository port it owns.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: MaintenanceRecord is a child of the equipment whose unit it describes, yet it has its own repository: RecordMaintenanceHandler adds records without loading Equipment, so nothing checks that the unit exists or belongs to any equipment, and Equipment cannot keep any rule that spans its units' maintenance.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The member repository contract returns a live IQueryable<Member>: callers compose arbitrary queries against the persistence provider, so the port leaks the ORM and its query translation limits into the application.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: fullName, email and phone travel together as three strings through Register, ChangeContactDetails and HasSameContact: the missing value object (contact details) leaves validation and equality of the three to every caller and lets them be passed in the wrong order.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The rule 'a member in good standing may borrow' (Status is Active AND the membership has not expired) is decided twice, in CheckoutEquipmentHandler and in ReservationService, over Member's Status and MembershipExpiresAt, and nowhere on Member. A change to the rule has to be found and made in both places.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: One command writes two aggregates in one unit of work: it adds the Loan and updates the Member (its lifetime loan counter). The member's consistency now depends on the loan transaction; the counter should follow from the LoanOpened event.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The public constructor stores a raw description and cost without checking them and the type offers no factory: a maintenance record with an empty description or a negative cost can be created and persisted.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: RenewMembership reads DateTimeOffset.UtcNow inside the aggregate: the new expiry cannot be tested at a chosen instant and differs from the time the command was accepted; every other domain method receives its instant.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Handling LoanOpened, Billing calls the catalogue's HTTP API to fetch the replacement value for the deposit. The consumer is coupled in time to the producer's availability (a catalogue outage stalls or fails deposit holds); the value belongs in the event, as the damage event already does.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: ExtendLoanCommand has two handlers: Lending's ExtendLoanHandler and Billing's ChargeExtensionFeeHandler. A command expresses one intent with one owner; Billing reacting to an extension should subscribe to an event.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A domain event named as an instruction (ExtendLoan) instead of a fact (LoanExtended): it reads as a command and invites consumers to treat it as a request that may be refused.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The handler commits the suspension and then publishes MemberSuspendedIntegrationEvent straight to the bus. A crash or bus failure between the two loses the event for good (Billing never learns of the suspension); the other handlers write their integration events through the outbox in the same transaction.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Each delivery of EquipmentDamageReported posts a new damage charge to the member's account. The bus delivers at least once and the handler keeps no record of processed message ids, so a redelivery charges the member twice.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The fold for LateFeeCharged stamps LastActivityAt with the wall clock instead of the event's ChargedAt, so rehydrating the same stream at a different time produces a different aggregate state.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The balance projection's fold for PaymentReceived stores the wall-clock time as the last payment time: rebuilding the read model from the same events gives different values. A projection fold is a fold.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A persisted event with public setters: code holding the event (or the in-memory store's reference to it) can rewrite the amount or reference of a payment that has already been recorded.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The first event of every account stream records the holder's full name and e-mail address in the append-only event store, with no crypto-shredding: erasing a member (EraseMemberPersonalData) cannot remove them from Billing's history.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: StorageLocation models a value (a branch and a shelf) but is a class with public setters and no value equality. Any holder can rewrite equipment.Location.Shelf in place, bypassing Equipment.Relocate (no EquipmentRelocated is raised and the change is saved silently by the owned-type mapping), and Equipment.Relocate's `Location == location` (Equipment.cs) compares references, so relocating to the same branch and shelf with a new instance is taken for a move and raises the event again. The line range runs from the type declaration to the setters.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Equipment.Relocate raises EquipmentRelocated so that members holding a reservation for the equipment are told where to collect it (the event's own documentation), but nothing handles it: IntegrationEventMapper maps only member and loan events, Lending has no in-process domain-event handler, and LendingDbContext clears the event after saving. Members with a reservation go to the old branch.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Member.ErasePersonalData raises MemberPersonalDataErased, but nothing subscribes to it and it is not mapped to an integration event, so Billing, which holds the member's name and e-mail (MemberAccountOpened, the account holder), is never told of the erasure and cannot act on it. An erasure request has to reach every recipient of the data (GDPR art. 17 and 19); the event that should carry it goes nowhere. Present since v1.0.0 and labelled in v1.1.0, when the concept was added to the taxonomy.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: DepositHeld is persisted in the account event store as JSON (AccountEventSerializer, since commit 9fe669e, with the property `loan`). Commit 96f0557 renamed the property Loan to LoanId without a new schema version or an upcaster (the serializer still registers deposit-held as version 1). A stored DepositHeld written before the rename has no `loanId`, so it deserialises with LoanId = default (an empty Guid): on replay every historical deposit is keyed by the same empty loan, MemberAccount.ReleaseDeposit no longer finds the real loan, and returned items never release their deposit. The previous commit (0afd2db) shows the established pattern, a version bump with an upcaster, for LateFeeCharged.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Billing's public balance query takes Lending's domain id (Rentals.Lending.Domain.Members.MemberId) instead of a primitive or a Billing type (commit e813432). Every caller of Billing's query API now compiles against Lending's domain model, and a change to Lending's member id is a breaking change for Billing's consumers. ADR 0005 (da7f315) states that a context's own types do not cross: Billing names members by the primitive id the contracts carry (MemberAccountId).
entries.subject: AccountBalanceQuery

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Billing's public handler implements ICommandHandler<ExtendLoanCommand>, a Lending application type (with Lending's LoanId and MemberId), so Billing's public surface is typed by Lending's internals rather than by the integration contracts (ADR 0005). Present since v1.0.0 (judged valid in iteration 1 as the coupling behind ED2-001) and labelled in v1.1.0, when the key covers boundary-type-leakage.
entries.subject: ChargeExtensionFeeHandler.HandleAsync

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Reservation refers to the member and the equipment by their strongly-typed ids, which is the aggregate-boundary rule followed, not broken (whatever else is wrong with Reservation).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Equipment holds its own child entities (the physical units). EquipmentUnit has identity and behaviour but is reached only through Equipment and has no repository: it is inside the boundary, not another aggregate.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Integration events cross a context boundary and carry ids as primitives on purpose, so consumers do not depend on the producer's id types.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Money is an immutable record in the shared kernel both contexts already depend on; carrying it couples no consumer to the producer's domain model.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A value object: data with value equality and a guarded constructor. It has no identity and no lifecycle, so 'no state-changing behaviour' is what it should have.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A read model written only by its projection and served to queries: a DTO, not an entity; it has no invariants of its own to protect.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Public setters on a read model that only the projection writes are the normal shape of a denormalised view.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Equipment's setters are private (EF Core materialises through them) and its units are exposed as a read-only view over a private list; all changes go through AddUnit, Rename, ChangeRates, ReportDamage and RetireUnit.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: EF Core mapping of a domain type, in the infrastructure project: infrastructure depending on the domain is the allowed direction.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A repository for the Loan aggregate root that returns materialised aggregates and lists, never a query handle.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The handler reads Equipment (for the replacement value it puts on the damage event) but writes only the Loan; the unit's condition follows from the published event in a separate transaction.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The public constructor validates its raw name (ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace) and receives the rates as Money, which validates itself.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The constructor takes only value objects (EquipmentUnitId, SerialNumber), each of which validated itself.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Generating a new identity with Guid.NewGuid is not a rule input: no domain decision depends on its value.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: SendAsync here puts a command on the message bus for the statements service; it is asynchronous messaging, not a request/response call to another service.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: An event with two subscribers (Billing charges the damage, Lending marks the unit damaged): fan-out is what events are for.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: 'Held' is the irregular past participle of 'hold': the name states a fact.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The outbox dispatcher publishes messages that were committed with the business change and then marks them dispatched; a crash in between republishes (at least once), it never loses one. This is the outbox.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The handler records each message id in the inbox and skips a message it has already processed, so a redelivered LoanReturned does not release the deposit or charge the late fee twice.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The new charge id is generated in the decision method and recorded in the event; the fold only copies it, so replay is deterministic.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: init-only properties: they can be set by an object initialiser when the event is created and never after.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: An integration message, not a stored event: it sits in the outbox only until it is dispatched (the row is then deleted) and is never appended to an event store.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The overdue rule lives on Loan, the type that owns the data; the overdue-loans query asks the loan rather than re-deciding it.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A readonly record struct: positional, init-only, with compiler-generated value equality. It is used as a dictionary key (MemberAccount's held deposits), which needs value equality and gets it; a struct and a positional record look like a mutable value to a careless rule, but `readonly` makes the property init-only.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: ChargePosted has no message handler and no integration event, but it is handled: MemberAccount folds it into the balance and AccountBalanceProjection.When(ChargePosted) applies it to the balance view (ProjectionRunner feeds the projection from the store's log). A projection is a subscriber.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: LateFeeCharged's stored shape changed after events of it were persisted (commit 0afd2db: the total `amount` was replaced by `dailyFee`), and the change was made correctly: the serializer registers late-fee-charged as schema version 2 and LateFeeChargedV1ToV2 lifts stored version-1 JSON (daily fee = total / days late) before it is deserialised; a test reads a literal version-1 event.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Money in Billing's public surface is the shared kernel, owned by neither context (ADR 0001 and ADR 0005: shared-kernel types cross freely); it couples Billing to Rentals.SharedKernel, which both contexts depend on by design, not to Lending.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Member data in Lending changes with no audit record; only Billing's event-sourced account keeps a full history of its (financial) changes. Partial at best.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Personal data (members, account events) is kept indefinitely: no retention period, TTL or purge job exists. Dispatched outbox rows are deleted, which is not a retention policy for personal data.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Erasure exists for Lending (EraseMemberPersonalData anonymises the member) but cannot reach Billing's event store (ES3-001); there is no export and no consent handling.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Genuine personal data is held in a handful of fields (member name, e-mail, phone; the account opening event's holder name and e-mail; the registration integration event).

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: The model uses value objects and typed ids throughout, with one real data clump (fullName/email/phone on Member, DM8-001). Mostly good, not perfect.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Of roughly a dozen mutating handlers, one consumer double-applies on redelivery (ED5-001); the others are guarded by an inbox, a lookup or a natural key, or set fixed values. Judged dimension: wide band.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Personal data (member contact details, account holder name and e-mail) is stored without encryption at rest and no data-protection or key-management API is used; encryption is left to the platform. Absent in code.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: One stored event type (MemberAccountOpened) carries a person's name and e-mail with no crypto-shredding; the other stored events carry ids and amounts only.
